name: Fix striking distance keywords from Google Search Console using rival pages from Bright Data, GPT-5.6 and Slack

parameters.content:
## Fix the keywords you almost rank for

Search Console knows which queries put you on page two. It cannot show you the pages that are beating you, because it only holds your own rows. This workflow reads the near misses, then goes and reads the competition.

### How it works

Two Search Console reports run each week over the same 28 day length, one recent and one a month older, both broken down by query and page. A code step keeps the rows inside your striking distance band - enough impressions to matter, ranked below the top few but still on the radar - and pairs each with its position a month ago, so a keyword that is climbing is told apart from one that is sliding.

One page usually owns a dozen wordings of the same keyword, so pages are grouped and only the strongest query from each survives. Without that, one page would consume the entire run.

Each surviving query is searched through Bright Data. The pages ranking above yours are collected, and Bright Data reads both theirs and yours. A model compares the heading structures and returns what they cover that you do not, plus one concrete change to make first.

Results land in a Google Sheet, one row per page, and a single digest goes to Slack.

### Setup

1. A Google service account credential, scoped to `webmasters.readonly`, added as a user on the property in Search Console.

2. Bright Data: a SERP API zone and a Web Unlocker zone. Their names go in **Settings**, along with your property and domain.

3. Google Sheets and Slack credentials.

4. Tune `min_impressions`, the position band and `max_pages`.

Runs weekly. The sheet and the Slack message are the only nodes that write anything.

## 1. Two windows of Search Console
Queries and pages for the last 28 days and for the 28 before. n8n has no Search Console node, so both go over HTTP.

## 2. What is nearly ranking
Rows inside the position band with enough impressions, grouped so one page cannot take the whole run with a dozen wordings of one keyword.

## 3. Who is above you
Bright Data searches each keyword, collects the pages ranking above yours, then reads both theirs and yours.

## 4. What they cover that you do not
Heading structures are compared rather than full articles. A model returns the gap and the one change to make first.

## 5. Log and tell the team
One sheet row per page, including the ones that could not be checked, and a single Slack digest.

## The service account needs adding in Search Console

n8n has no Search Console node, so this uses a Google service account over HTTP. Enabling the API in Cloud grants nothing on its own: add the account's email as a user on the property in Search Console, or every fetch returns 403.
